rationale: Manipulated weather and traffic feeds can cause widespread flight conflicts and unsafe routing with potentially catastrophic consequences.
Strategic information disclosure can expose operational weaknesses and enable future attacks, but does not directly compromise flight safety.
Poisoning the SSOT can simultaneously corrupt dependent services across the federation, causing systemic failures and potentially catastrophic aviation accidents.
Manipulated altitude data and inertial measurements can directly destabilize flight control, cause collisions, and produce catastrophic crashes.
Injected positions can conceal genuine traffic conflicts and create phantom aircraft, undermining separation and potentially causing catastrophic collisions.
Tampered audit trails obstruct incident investigation and accountability, indirectly increasing safety risk without directly disrupting flight operations.
Exploiting regulatory gaps can permit inadequately secured USSP operations at scale, creating serious systemic safety and oversight deficiencies.
Spoofed identities and stolen credentials enable unauthorized operations that undermine operator accountability and can create serious airspace safety risks.
Bypassing authorization controls can enable unrestricted unauthorized flights throughout a managed volume, potentially causing catastrophic conflicts and collisions.
Removing no-fly zone boundaries can systematically authorize flights into restricted airspace, potentially causing catastrophic encounters with crewed aircraft or hazardous sites.
GNSS spoofing or jamming can divert multiple aircraft into hazardous airspace or cause loss of navigation, resulting in potentially catastrophic accidents.
Sabotage of critical vertiport controls or physical landing areas can endanger aircraft and people during approach, landing, or ground operations.
Compromised geofencing can mislead multiple operators into restricted airspace, creating potentially catastrophic encounters with protected or crewed-aircraft areas.
Backdoored flight controllers or malicious firmware can compromise flight integrity across deployed aircraft and cause uncontrolled flight or catastrophic crashes.
Tampered regulatory audit records can conceal unsafe USSP practices and prevent corrective enforcement, creating moderate indirect safety consequences.
A compromised trusted supplier can distribute persistent backdoors across an entire fleet, enabling widespread loss of aircraft integrity and catastrophic safety failures.
Ground infrastructure outages can halt operations, while malicious battery depletion during flight can cause power loss and catastrophic aircraft crashes.
Flooding a single API gateway can disrupt authorizations across an entire operational volume, creating serious safety risks through loss of essential services.
SQL injection can expose and corrupt large volumes of flight-plan data, degrading operational integrity and creating moderate safety consequences.
Jamming or compromising command-and-control links can cause loss of aircraft control during BVLOS flight, potentially resulting in catastrophic crashes.
Bulk exfiltration of sensitive flight plans compromises operational confidentiality and can facilitate targeted attacks, with indirect and generally minor immediate safety consequences.
